options.text: Only the animals that live in an area
A single species and its offspring
All the living and nonliving parts of an area
A large region with many different climates

items.explanation: An ecosystem is all of the living (biotic) and nonliving (abiotic) parts of the environment in a given area.

items.stem: Which of the following is a biotic factor?
items.explanation: Biotic factors are living or once-living. A lizard is alive. Sunlight, soil, and temperature are abiotic.

items.stem: Which of these would be an abiotic factor in a pond?
items.explanation: Abiotic factors are nonliving. Water temperature is nonliving, while fish, algae, and frogs are all living.

items.stem: Which level of organization is the smallest?
items.explanation: A single organism is the smallest level. From there it builds up to population, community, ecosystem, and biome.

items.stem: All of the different populations living together in one area make up a what?
items.explanation: A community is all the populations of different species living together in the same area at the same time.

items.stem: A coyote's habitat is best described as its what?

options.text: Home, the place that meets its needs
Job, the role it plays in the ecosystem

items.explanation: A habitat is the place where an organism lives and finds what it needs. Its role or job is its niche.

items.stem: A coyote hunts and eats a jackrabbit. This interaction is an example of what?
items.explanation: Predation is when one organism, the predator, feeds on another organism, its prey. The coyote is the predator.

items.stem: The Joshua tree and the yucca moth both benefit from their relationship. What type of symbiosis is this?
items.explanation: When both species benefit from a close, long-term relationship, the symbiosis is mutualism.

items.stem: A tick feeds on a deer, harming the deer while the tick benefits. This is an example of what?
items.explanation: In parasitism, one species (the parasite) benefits while the other (the host) is harmed. The tick harms the deer.

items.stem: Two coyotes both try to catch the same jackrabbit. This interaction is an example of what?
items.explanation: Competition happens when two or more organisms need the same resource at the same time, such as the same prey.
